title: Propagate intermediate sizes into component bounds
obstacle: A later call receives a larger encoding or longer operands than the original inputs used in a preliminary estimate.
procedure: Specify the size measure at each boundary and bound the output of each relevant component.
Substitute that size into the next cost envelope where monotonicity or a uniform estimate permits it.
For a space bound, account for caller data still live, temporary storage and any recomputation.
verification: Follow one complete composition and check all size substitutions and units at the actual calls.
positive_example: If a component can double an operand length, charge the following multiplication for its new bit length.
negative_example: Bounding each child by the original input length can lose a growing intermediate; adding net allocations does not bound peak live storage.

evidence.note: General design guidance. Check its conditions in the current argument; no comparative performance claim.
